lede: The biggest thing this week is a public vote on who leads Telluride Regional Medical Center — the board meets in special session, takes public comment, and comes out of executive session to name interim leadership, which is about as consequential as a single meeting gets. Alongside that, Telluride Town Council takes up a deed-restriction conversion that would remove the price cap on two affordable units at 215 East Colorado Avenue, Mountain Village considers shifting housing authority fees out of municipal code into an annually updated schedule, and the Comprehensive Plan update gets a Phase 2 community engagement check-in. Blues & Brews kicks off Thursday and runs through the weekend.

notable.stake: Board votes publicly on who leads the regional medical center.
Vote to remove price caps on two affordable units; three public hearings on second reading.
Resolution converts two deed-restricted ownership units to employee dwelling units, removing sale price limits.
First reading shifts MVHA affordable housing fees out of municipal code, changing how costs get set.
Comp Plan Phase 2 engagement review shapes long-range land use and density decisions for Telluride.
